commissioned_by: Paul Kilty, 24 September 2026 ("ok can you write them please"), after the London gap review
run_by: Opus session run from the brief on 24 September 2026, branch discovery/london-boroughs-2026-09-24
budget: No Anthropic API call from this session. Pages read by direct curl; hosts that refused curl (brent.gov.uk, camden.gov.uk, lbhf.gov.uk, walthamforest.gov.uk, rbkc.gov.uk, groundwork.org.uk, peabody.org.uk, camdengiving.org.uk, crowdfunder.co.uk) were read through the keyless reader proxy r.jina.ai, which answered today. barnet.gov.uk and lbbd.gov.uk refused both and are listed for Paul’s browser.
dedup: Full read of scraped_grants (2,181 rows, count asserted equal before any comparison), by funder name and normalised apply URL, per candidate before drafting. The staging script re-read the whole table and refuses on URL or exact-title collision unless a row declares a deliberate shared URL (Hounslow council grants page, EECF Tower Hamlets page, H&F small grants page).
scoring_method: Dashboard gates in order (canonical funding type, legal structure, sector intersection, grantMatchesLocationText on location_tag), then computeMatchScore; 55+ counts. Canary rows prove the scorer can say yes (92) and no (location gate). Second derivation: scripts/preview-staged-activation.ts over the stored rows agrees on the same three pairs; stored rows score 3 points higher than the in-memory draft rows (69/65/82 vs 66/62/79).

totals.why_so_few_reach: Five of the eight named organisations have primary_location "London" (2-3 Degrees x2 records, Expert Impact, Blue Garage, Unicorn Theatre, Bikeworks CIC), so the dashboard location gate stops every borough-tagged row from reaching them; only London-wide rows can. Of the three borough-located orgs, Paws and Pause is reached by Sir Walter St John’s (Lambeth); Asian Community Concern’s newer record by the Elizabeth line fund, its older record not (44, niche-tag specialism dampen); Institute of Imagination is capped at 35 on Lyle’s Local Fund because its profile sets a £20,000 minimum grant and the fund tops out at £5,000.

scoring_notes.title: Scoring notes before staging
scoring_notes.note: Lyle’s Local Fund retagged from the brochure themes (added education, creative) after the heritage keyword tripped the specialist-domain veto for Institute of Imagination; it still scores 35 because IoI’s profile sets a £20,000 minimum and the fund tops out at £5,000 (the matcher caps below-minimum grants at 35). Better Spaces scores 44 for Asian Community Concern because it is a building energy fund, correctly weak for a women’s employment CIC. WCGL Community Ideas had a max_org_income of £50,000 that was stricter than the page (income under £50,000 OR grants under £10,000); removed.
